mentl/2a9c075:
warm-inc traps, and the root is the uniform bracket meeting the persisted
globals. Pinned at the instruction rather than inferred: 0x4a589 in
driver_warm_persist is `call ev_declaring_node` with i32.const 100764 =
Persist, slot 0. Diagnostic and Filesystem resolve after the restore; Persist
does not.

image_pack snapshots the globals and $world_g is one of them. Packed from
inside persist_to_disk's own arm, the world it captures is the ARM's — which
by the deep-handler law excludes the very handler doing the packing. Run 1
therefore wrote an image whose world cannot answer `persist`, and run 2
restored it and performed `persist` against that chain. Before the bracket
was uniform the arm still had its own handler in view, so the wire happened
to record a chain that worked.

THE FIX IS A DECOMPOSITION, not a world patch. `persist = memcpy` is the
SUBSTRATE operation and is identical for every handler that could answer the
op; what a handler chooses is where the bytes land. The file already said so
— "This handler IS the disk policy" — while the arm did the packing anyway.
The op takes the WIRE now, packing runs at the perform site, and the handler
writes what it was handed. The world comes out right as a consequence:
the caller's chain still contains persist_to_disk, so the restored image can
answer the op that wrote it.

persist_write survives with exactly one caller, persist_branch, whose pack
CANNOT move: it checkpoints before invoking the branch, at a path derived
from handler state. That arm still records a world without its own handler,
which is Hβ.persist.branch-world-tag precisely — an already-named peer that
now has the measurement it never had.

mentl/2af1a46:
Two load-bearing correctness fixes, both Carried-Truth violations:

1. UNIFY TVar FIX (src/infer.mn + bootstrap/src/infer/unify.wat)
   unify_types's TVar arm called graph_bind(ha, b) without first chasing ha.
   When ha was already bound (a lambda arg's (r)->ret proven by inference),
   the raw bind overwrote the existing proof — discarding it, orphaning r, so
   a concrete payload record never met r and the record never closed. Fix:
   chase ha live; if already bound, unify b against the existing binding —
   never overwrite. Byte-identical for the common free-var case; eliminates
   the field-access-lambda trap (config-handler HOF lambdas: 134 exits → 2).
   Applied in both layers (wheel + seed).

2. EFFECTS REFACTOR (src/effects.mn + own.mn + pipeline.mn + types.mn)
   Hand-rolled comparators (eff_name_lt, effect_eq, etc.) replaced with
   structural == throughout — −253 lines net. The refactor is load-bearing:
   HEAD trapped in eff_name_lt (the null-trap it targeted); the refactor
   marches the trap forward. Verified: 7/7 micros byte-identical, drift-audit
   clean, m2 builds + assembles (184150 bytes).

mentl/2aa690a:
The deep substrate-architectural realization the session surfaced:
lower's "unknown name → LGlobal" silent fallback was drift. LGlobal
served two semantically distinct meanings — "name resolved as
top-level binding" AND "I gave up resolving this" — collapsed onto
one LowExpr tag. ~600 wat2wasm "undefined global" errors at the
residue level traced to this overloading.

Substrate fix per protocol_no_silent_fallback.md (NEW protocol
crystallized 2026-05-08): introduce LUnresolved (tag 335) as an
EXPLICIT LowExpr sentinel for genuinely-unresolved names. Lower's
$lower_var_ref step 3 now distinguishes:
  - $ls_is_global(name) true → LGlobal (real top-level binding)
  - else → LUnresolved (genuinely unknown)

Emit's $emit_lunresolved arm projects to:
  ;; UNRESOLVED: <name>
  (unreachable)

Valid WAT — wat2wasm accepts (unreachable); runtime traps if
execution reaches the site; preserves L1 closure even amid
wheel-source dangling references (TFree, TCapability, sin, tanh,
cache_pack_byte, etc. — wheel is in pre-production state with
many missing constructor / fn definitions; the seed now compiles
the wheel without rejecting it for the wheel author's incompleteness).

Empirical:
  Pre:  608 wat2wasm errors / 582 undef-globals
  Post:  41 wat2wasm errors /  15 undef-globals (-93% of remaining)
  Total cumulative: 3708 → 41 (-98.9%) in 9 substrate moves this session.
  Wheel-out: 2862 ;; UNRESOLVED sentinels — surfaceable as compile-
  time diagnostics without blocking compilation.

Eight interrogations on "what does the ULTIMATE MEDIUM do for
unresolved names":
  1. Graph?     env_lookup returned 0; substrate carries this fact
                explicitly via the new tag.
  2. Handler?   Diagnostic handler can fire on LUnresolved at
                compile-time; runtime trap fires if execution
                reaches the site.
  3. Verb?      Unresolved is a graph edge from use-site to a
                "no-binding" sentinel; cursor projects it as Reason.
  4. Row?       Reso

The shipped APK's libapp.so carried 21.4 MiB of symbol and debug
sections (69.0 -> 46.6 MiB under eu-strip, measured against the
apk-latest release) — mostly std's prebuilt debuginfo linking into a
profile that never asked for any. strip = "symbols" removes it at
link time. The determinism matrix runs the dev profile, so release
symbols never feed a checksum; the panic hook reports source
locations from panic metadata, which stripping does not touch. A
device install of the next CI APK is the remaining operator check.
clob/2a7ed67:
Run the pre-registered equal-compute Bet 2 test on the Phase 6 QAT
step-15000 substrate. The substrate reproduces Phase 6 bit-identically
(cleared holdout NLL 3.797228), so crystal-dense's cleared arm agrees
with eval-dense --ternary and the validity precondition holds.

Verdict: KILL, robustly, by two distinct mechanisms. On the deployed
ternary core the trained core's high-error episodes crystallize zero
distillable modules across the entire registered grid (n_clusters
8/16/32, causal on/off, activation threshold 0.3/0.5/0.7); every
candidate cluster fails the distiller's coherence or MDL gate, because a
trained core's surprising tokens are spread across too many next-tokens
to form a coherent correction. With no modules, loaded equals cleared,
delta 0, which trips the registered kill line. On the f32-latent core two
modules do form and reduce held-out capability by 3.611% — the
overfit-and-drift failure the bet names. The drift line passes by
construction: untouched tokens are scored from the identical hidden in
both arms.

This is the first crystallization test on a substrate that can learn;
every prior run was on a random core. It supersedes those whisper
results. The kill is a finding about the loop as built, not a proof no
variant can work; the capture threshold and the distill target are the
named suspects, each for its own future pre-registered run. Bet 2 in
ARCHITECTURE.md moves to a measured kill; PLAN.md, IF_FOUND.md, and the
Path B build doc record it and fork the next gate.
